starting_point: Some data engineering or infrastructure experience, plus basic Linux, SQL and Git. This is an adjacent transition for many learners.
mapping_note: A workshop combination of Data Engineer and DevOps topics. No separate Data Platform Engineer roadmap is claimed.

phase_1.label: Define a small shared platform
phase_1.slide: A platform diagram, user needs and access model
actions: Describe two fictional teams that need isolated datasets and a shared onboarding process.
Design a local PostgreSQL setup, two roles and a simple metadata register. Learn authentication versus authorisation.
phase_1.output: An architecture sketch, access matrix and repeatable local setup.

phase_2.label: Create a reusable onboarding route
phase_2.slide: Two isolated teams using the same setup template
actions: Automate creation of schemas, read/write roles and one sample dataset per team.
Add basic health checks and record dataset owner, purpose, schema and refresh expectations.
phase_2.output: An onboarding template, sample catalog and usage instructions.

phase_3.label: Test operation and handover
phase_3.slide: Access checks, restore evidence and a user guide
actions: Verify allowed and denied access for each role, then run a backup-and-restore exercise.
Ask another person to onboard a third fictional team using your template and capture friction.
phase_3.output: A small platform starter with operational evidence and an improvement backlog.

portfolio: A local data platform starter for two fictional teams, with separate access and reusable onboarding.
tools: PostgreSQL, shell or Python scripts, Git, and optional local containers. Cloud deployment is optional.
acceptance: Two fictional teams can use their own data, and documented tests deny cross-team access.
One setup command or script reproduces the platform and sample datasets.
A restore exercise recovers the sample data and the runbook records the steps and measured recovery time.
first_step: Draw who owns each dataset and which role may read or change it.
beginner_adjustment: Start with PostgreSQL roles and one schema. Defer cloud networking, Kubernetes and vendor-specific governance tooling.
